text:
hana: Putting the shared embed helper into the sample-rerank flow and CI blew up. Assertion: expected (6,1536) got (6,768). Anyone familiar with mixed vec sizes?

peter: Which aliases and SDKs? Node or Python?

hana: Node sample uses node-sdk default alias open-embed-compact -> 768 dims. Py sample uses open-embed-standard -> 1536 dims. The helper assumes STANDARD.

li: Two things we've seen before: SDK default alias drift and inconsistent response field names (`embedding` vs `vector`). Both lead to stack shape errors in rerank.

hana: Sample CI failure snippet: `AssertionError stacker.py: expected (6,1536) got (6,768)` Logs show node response body with key `vector` and 768 floats. Py response `embedding` 1536 floats.

build-bot: CI: samples/rerank-onboard #834 failed — see job logs (sanitized).

sam: Short-term fix: add normalize_embed(resp) in the shared helper that: 1) picks `embedding` then `vector`, 2) converts to `embedding` key, 3) pads or trims to expected_dim with a clear error message if off by a lot.

jo: Long-term: SDKs must have parity on default alias, and server should standardize response schema. Also infra should ensure retry paths preserve idempotency headers so duplicate arrivals don't confuse the aggregator.

hana: I pushed a small sample patch: samples/onboard/normalize-embed + README note about alias sizes. PR link in thread. Unblocks demos.

sam: I'll add a CI matrix test that calls every embed alias from node+py and records (field_name, dim) and fails if mismatch. Will also auto-open a parity issue.

li: Filed infra ticket for idempotency header preservation on token-refresh retries. Without it we sometimes see duplicate responses with different fields.

peter: Good plan. Also add a friendly onboarding check snippet: `assert len(embedding) == EXPECTED_DIM, f\"expected {EXPECTED_DIM} got {len(embedding)} (alias mismatch)\"` so users see a clear error.

hana: Thanks. Will keep the normalize shim in samples until SDK parity lands. :thumbsup:
